campaign.target: complete Phase-G Rust, Python, and CLI extraction surface

findings.description: A dotted Jinja-looking expression is accepted as a literal variable identifier during known-template XML extraction. The behavior is deterministic, but the Phase-G contract does not say whether dotted text means a literal variable name or object-path access.
findings.expected_behavior: The worker oracle expected dotted attribute syntax to be rejected with ERR_EXTRACT_UNSUPPORTED.

replay.result: same accepted literal variable and diagnostic on all three replays

findings.requirement_adr_trace: FR-16 and ADR-0011 define a documented scalar XML subset but do not define dotted-expression semantics. VariableName::new explicitly permits dots, while extraction does not promise reconstruction of object attributes.
findings.requirement_follow_up: Team lead/product owner should decide whether dotted expressions are literal variable names or object-path expressions, then amend FR-16/ADR-0011 and add a contract test if needed.
findings.recommended_change: Clarify the contract before changing implementation. Do not reject or reinterpret dotted names solely from this fuzz result.
findings.classification_reason: The worker's unsupported-syntax oracle conflicts with the existing public VariableName validation contract, and no Phase-G requirement resolves the ambiguity. This is not sufficient evidence for a confirmed defect.

unresolved_candidates.next_action: Decide literal dotted-variable versus object-path semantics and update FR-16/ADR-0011 plus a contract test if the decision changes behavior.
